Yeah, I think this was another bug introduced in 2706c5b7c8eee7ffd8c3b23a8012f346165ddb93? It dropped the NONPREF_PEER_TX_DELAY sleep.

Not sure if there is another test case already for the outbound announcing first, but I think it would be good to write two test cases, or at a minimum fix this test case to add back the `NONPREF_PEER_TX_DELAY` properly.

[2026-11-25] rc:4699767011 inline on test/functional/p2p_tx_download.py by Crypt-iQ (member) (edited 2026-11-25):
I tested that commit and it did introduce the bug. I modified the test to use mocktime and request from a blocking inbound peer first in 4cc74b2b602d6b64364b91e1e8f9768f78d21b6d. I decided against adding a subtest for an outbound announcing first since `test_preferred_tiebreaker_inv` covers this case and, to me, it doesn't really test a peer blocking relay. It mostly seems like an artifact of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/2706c5b7c8eee7ffd8c3b23a8012f346165ddb93. Also, the whole `p2p_tx_download.py` suite takes ~20s to run on my machine, compared to the commit before https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/2706c5b7c8eee7ffd8c3b23a8012f346165ddb93 which took ~90s to run.

Latest push to 4cc74b2b602d6b64364b91e1e8f9768f78d21b6d uses mocktime and ensures that `self.nodes[1]` requests from a blocking inbound peer first. It is also slightly faster. I will run the patch under `rr` and see if I've introduced any flakes.
